One sheet of paper is  $9\times10^{-3}$cm thick.

Mark wants to put $500$sheets of paper into the paper tray of his printer. 
The paper tray is $4$ cm deep.

Is the paper tray deep enough for $500$ sheets of paper?

parts.solution_md:
> *Identify the calculation you will need to work out.*

*Thickness of 500 sheets = 500 × thickness of one sheet = 500 × (9 × 10**<sup>-3</sup>**)*

> *Evaluate by multiplying 9 by 500.*

*500 × 9 × 10**<sup>-3 </sup>**= 4500 × 10**<sup>-3</sup>*

**[1]**

> *This is not in standard form as **a** is not in the interval 1 ≤ **a **< 10. Convert to standard form by first converting 4500 to standard form.*

*4500 × 10**<sup>-3 </sup>**= 4.5 × 10**<sup>3</sup>** × 10**<sup>-3</sup>*

**[1]**

> *Simplify using the law of indices **a*<sup>*m*</sup>* **×** a*<sup>*n *</sup>*= **a*<sup>*m+n*</sup>*.*

*Thickness of 500 sheets = 4.5 × 10**<sup>3-3 </sup>**= 4.5 × 10**<sup>0</sup>**  = 4.5 × 1 = 4.5 cm*

**No, the paper tray is not deep enough as 500 sheets are 4.5 cm thick ****[1]**
